specials.text: Scratched into the stone at the dead end: THE DEAD KEEP WHAT IS THEIRS.

captives.text: Two grave robbers are binding a struggling grave-digger.

specials.text: Old bones are heaped against the wall, picked clean.
A dead orc courier lies here, a satchel of orders under him. One names the Ruinfield Gate, and the countersign its garrison asks for.
The gate stands open. Cut into the lintel in the old script: HOLD UNTIL RELIEVED.

captives.text: A beastman deserter is chained in the stables, and two warbreed hounds are kept hungry beside him.

garrisons.text: Three old goblins stand to in the gatehouse, spears level, as if the war never ended.
Two orc guards hold the keep hall, their armor patched with twenty years of scrap.

specials.text: Nailed to the armory door: the last orders of Ashgate's commander, with the countersign the garrison was to accept from its relief.

garrisons.text: Ashgate's captain guards the archive himself, a guard at his side.

specials.text: Goats fill the yard, bellies swollen. In four months these pens will hold beastmen.
{pc} knows the smell of this place, though {pc} was born somewhere like it, not here.

captives.text: A slaver and two beastman troopers are dragging an old-breed goblin toward the cull rooms.

specials.text: Glass vats as tall as an orc line the hall. Most are cracked; something moved in the last whole one.
Under the laboratory bench, wrapped in oilcloth: the vat-master's working notes.
Bones fill the room to the knee: orcs and goblins of breeds no longer made.
Ledgers fill the shelves: every breed of orc and goblin the vats made, and the day each older breed was culled.
{pc} finds the orc lines. {pc}'s own breed is marked for the cull, the order signed but never carried out.
{pc} finds the goblin lines. {pc}'s breed is listed as a failure, kept for labor until a better one was ready.
In the officers' quarters, a brass token hangs on a hook by the door, waiting for whoever has the watch.
Records of the civil wars fill the map room: which lieutenant betrayed which, and when. Vael is in none of them as a traitor.

garrisons.text: Two clockwork servitors stand to beside their bunks, as they have every morning for twenty years.
A clockwork soldier guards the stair down to the command deck.

specials.text: Maps of a war that ended twenty years ago cover the walls, and someone still moves the pins each morning.
Orders in Vael's hand, dated every day for twenty years: hold the line, await the Dark Lord's word.
In the vault lies the Seal of Command, the Dark Lord's own, left with his most trusted lieutenant.

garrisons.text: The Iron Golem stands at the war room door, and turns its head.
Lieutenant Vael, an elf in a uniform twenty years old, bars the vault door. "You are not my relief," he says.

specials.text: The stockade is new timber over old stone. Fresh beastmen drill in the yard, none of them a year old.
Herd after herd of pregnant goats. Grisk has an army due within the year.
The crafter's writing desk holds a bound book: herbs, doses, and the words of the training.

captives.text: Two troopers keep the warlord's crafter at her work.

specials.text: A throne of old siege timber stands under the banners of three dead lieutenants.
Ember-red banners hang over the nave. The hymn painted on the wall asks the Dark Lord to come home, and promises him an army when he does.
A pilgrim's slate hangs by the vestry door, chalked with the words the guards on the Throne Road want to hear: "The night keeps faith."
Carts stand ready in the yard, loaded with shrouded bodies and pointed north.

captives.text: Faithful acolytes are loading the dead onto carts. An old orc woman screams at them to give her husband back.

specials.text: Niche after niche stands empty. The Lady's priests laid these dead to rest a hundred years ago; someone has taken every one.
Among the empty niches {pc} finds name-plates in the old tongue of the homeland: elders deported and buried here, and now taken too.
Shelves of deportation rolls, a thousand years of them. Somewhere here {pc} finds a family name they were told never to speak.
The breeding ledgers of the empire, shelf on shelf. Whole breeds of goblin are entered here and struck out in a single line.
A reading desk, still laid out for a clerk: ink, sand, and an order to the Saltgate dated the day the capital fell.

garrisons.text: Three clockwork scribes step out from the stacks and hold out their hands for your pass.

specials.text: On a Faithful clerk's desk lies the watchword they give the Citadel's bound: "The throne waits."

A spy's ledger of the alliance's plans against the Dark Lord: three hundred and twelve of them, each struck through as it failed, but one. That page has been cut out, long ago, with a very sharp knife.

garrisons.text: A clockwork soldier guards the sealed stacks, with two scribes behind it.

specials.text: Barracks for a thousand. The bunks are made, and the bound who keep them sleep in shifts beside the gate they have kept for twenty years.

garrisons.text: Bound orcs in the Dark Lord's livery fill the gate passage. "The watchword," their captain says.
A war-engine squats at the head of the stair down, and an orc captain stands at its shoulder.

specials.text: Petitions to the Dark Lord, ten deep on every table. The last are dated the day his will left the world. None was answered.
The Faithful have chalked the floor for a rite: a circle of the Lady's dead around an empty chair, and a name left blank.

captives.text: Faithful zealots stand over a chained Priest of Death. Their keeper turns: "She is for the rite. You are not."

specials.text: The Dark Lord's throne stands empty. Dust lies undisturbed on the seat, twenty years of it, and in the arm is set a gnome-made device that still hums, as if listening for something that never comes.
